description: FLEURS (Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech) is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. It provides natural human speech and high quality transcripts, and can be used for a variety of speech tasks including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification, Translation and Retrieval.

name: FLEURS
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 recordings per sentence (by three different native speakers)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each sentence was recorded by three different native speakers. After recording, each recording was evaluated by additional workers to assess whether the recording corresponds to the input sentence. Invalid recordings were discarded, leaving between zero and three recordings per sentence. A sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% was imposed when possible. Speakers are disjoint between train/dev and test sets.
rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on the Western European group than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African or South Asian, which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages. The dataset imposes a sex ratio balance of at least 30/70% when possible. Speakers are disjoint between train/dev and test sets to avoid overfitting on speaker ID for LangID tasks.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built on top of FLoRes-101, which contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia translated into 101 languages by human translators. The dev and devtest sets (2009 sentences total) were split into new train/dev/test splits (1509/150/350 sentences). For each sentence in 102 languages, three recordings were collected from three different native speakers, with a target sex ratio balance of at least 30/70%. Each recording was then evaluated by additional workers to assess validity; invalid recordings were discarded. The speech sampling rate is 16kHz.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: About 21.5% of sentences are missing in the first version because none of the three recordings were validated. The authors plan to fill these gaps in future versions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source text data comes from FLoRes-101, which contains sentences extracted from English Wikipedia translated into 101 languages by human translators. Speech recordings were collected from native speakers at 16kHz sampling rate.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: About 21.5% of sentences are missing in the first version because none of the three recordings were validated. All recordings are kept as-is from quiet or noisy environments without any data augmentations. The dataset covers only 102 languages, and performance gaps exist across geographical groups, particularly for low-resource languages.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For textual data, NFC and FST normalization was applied to each sentence, followed by lower-casing, normalization and removal of punctuations. Words were split into characters with token 'j' used as word boundaries. Three versions of each sentence are provided: the original raw transcript (SRC_RAW), the preprocessed version (SRC_NORM), and its character-based version (SRC_CHAR). All segments are within 30 seconds.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to fill missing data gaps in future versions of the dataset.
rai:dataSocialImpact: FLEURS aims to enable speech technology in more languages, particularly low-resource ones, and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding, with the goal of building speech technologies for everyone.
rai:dataUseCases: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Speech-to-Text and Speech-to-Speech Translation, Multilingual Speech-to-Speech and Speech-to-Text Retrieval, and few-shot learning evaluation of multilingual speech representations.

null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: The paper only mentions native speakers with a sex ratio balance requirement but does not provide detailed annotator demographics such as age, nationality breakdown, or other demographic information.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement metrics or formal annotation quality analysis are reported in the paper beyond the validation/discard process.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The paper does not specify the annotation platform used for collecting recordings or validating them.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe or date range for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described; missing recordings are simply discarded rather than imputed.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The paper explicitly states no data augmentations were applied to the recordings.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: No machine annotation tools are described for the dataset creation process; human workers validated recordings.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper does not discuss collection of personal or sensitive information about speakers beyond sex ratio balance.

evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: The goal of FLEURS is to enable speech technology in more languages and catalyze research in low-resource speech understanding. evidence.rai:dataBiases: We observe in Table 4 that results are much better on the Western European group (with 10.7 and 10.6 average CER) than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African (15.6 and 16.4 average CER) or South Asian (17.4 and 19.2), which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages from MLS and VoxPopuli.
